text:
sanjay: quick idea — introduce per-model-family "lease windows" for burst credits. each org/key can request a short-lived lease that grants X tokens for a TTL. goal: let teams burst on expensive models without permanently raising steady-state quotas.

maria: nice. high-level question — who grants the lease? console, API, or an ops UI? also how do we present remaining burst to customers? :thinking_face:

alex: telemetry first: we need to emit lease_id, org_id, model_family, granted_tokens, tokens_consumed (per-model call), granted_ts, expiry_ts. make it easy to backfill billing and alerting.

taylor: enforcement point matters. if gateway rejects on lease exhaustion we get low-latency 429s. but runtime has exact token accounting (kv cache hits, prefix reuse). i'd prefer hybrid: gateway does fast pre-check using cached lease state, runtime authoritatively deducts and periodically reconciles.

sanjay: agreed. sketch of API: POST /v1/leases {"model_family":"gptx-8k","requested_tokens":20000,"ttl_secs":900} -> 200 {"lease_id":"l_abc123","granted":15000,"ttl":600} or 429 w/ suggested ttl. can put default weights per family so larger models cost more.

maria: console UX: show lease bar and countdown, link to usage by route (embedding vs generation). allow ops to grant manual emergency leases and revoke. also surface projected exhaustion based on current burn rate.

alex: on telemetry sampling — we should tag traces with lease_id. add a metric lease_tokens_remaining{org,model_family,lease_id}. aggregate to predict 5-min exhaustion and generate alert.

taylor: open question: variant fallbacks. if request pins to family A but we route to fallback family B (smaller/larger), which lease to charge? i vote: always charge the actual served family, but cost normalize using weight_table so it subtracts weighted tokens from the requested family's lease to avoid gaming.

sanjay: example weight table: {"gptx-32k":4, "gptx-8k":2, "gptx-2k":1} so a call on 32k subtracts 4x tokens from lease_quota if you want strict enforcement.

taylor: proto config YAML for console & gateway:
```yaml
leases:
  default_ttl_secs: 600
  max_request_tokens: 100000
  family_weights:
    gptx-32k: 4
    gptx-8k: 2
    gptx-2k: 1
  allow_manual_grant: true
```

maria: alerts: create dashboard with per-org per-family burn rate + a forecast line. add alert: predicted_depletion_minutes < 5 => PagerDuty for SRE, in-app banner for customer.

alex: billing/ledger: reconcile every minute from runtime deltas. if gateway pre-check granted but runtime later denies (race or reconcile), emit lease_reconcile event and refund/adjust ledger.

ops-bot: test-deploy: lease-service v0.7 deployed to staging (canary) — hit /v1/leases with 10k tokens and ttl 300s for org test-org.

sanjay: next steps: 1) prototype gateway pre-check + runtime reconciliation (taylor + alex). 2) add telemetry fields + example alerts (alex). 3) mock console widget + manual grant flow (maria). i'll write an RFC this week with the API examples and reconciliation semantics. thanks! :thumbsup:
